title.value: DR3: VALUE-BASED DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING REQUIRES EXPLICIT REGULARIZATION
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the paper on Deep Reinforcement Learning and the introduction of explicit regularization called DR3.
title.quote: In this paper, we discuss how the implicit regularization effect of SGD seen in supervised learning could in fact be harmful in the offline deep RL setting, leading to poor generalization and degenerate feature representations.

analysis.description: This paper examines the role of implicit regularization in deep reinforcement learning, particularly focusing on the offline setting. It highlights how the implicit regularization effect observed in supervised learning through stochastic gradient descent can lead to poor generalization and feature representation in reinforcement learning environments. To counteract this, the authors propose an explicit regularizer called DR3, which aims to improve the performance and stability of offline reinforcement learning by mitigating undesirable effects such as feature co-adaptation and rank collapse.

type.justification: The paper's focus is on theoretically analyzing the implicit regularization effects in deep reinforcement learning and proposing a new explicit regularizer, DR3, based on this theoretical understanding.
type.quote: Our theoretical analysis shows that when existing models of implicit regularization are applied to temporal difference learning, the resulting derived regularizer favors degenerate solutions with excessive 'aliasing', in stark contrast to the supervised learning case.

name.justification: The paper's analysis and contributions are within the context of reinforcement learning, specifically deep reinforcement learning with a focus on offline settings.
name.quote: Our goal is to understand the underlying cause of the emergence of poor representations during bootstrapping and develop a potential solution.

name.justification: The paper discusses the problems of poor feature representation and how to resolve it using explicit regularization.
name.quote: Our theoretical analysis shows that when existing models of implicit regularization are applied to temporal difference learning, the resulting derived regularizer favors degenerate solutions with excessive 'aliasing'.

name.justification: DR3 is explicitly introduced in this paper as a new regularization model for value-based deep reinforcement learning.
name.quote: ...we propose a simple and effective explicit regularizer, called DR3, that counteracts the undesirable effects of this implicit regularizer.

is_contributed.justification: DR3 is presented as a novel contribution in this paper to address the limitations identified in typical implicit regularization methods in deep reinforcement learning.
is_contributed.quote: Our first contribution is the derivation of the implicit regularizer that arises when training deep net value functions via TD learning...and DR3, which minimizes the feature similarity...

is_executed.justification: The execution details indicate theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations rather than specific execution environments like GPU or CPU.
is_executed.quote: We back up these findings empirically, showing that feature representations learned by a deep network value function trained via bootstrapping can indeed become degenerate... Empirically, using DR3 in conjunction with existing offline RL methods...

is_compared.justification: DR3 is empirically compared against existing offline RL methods, demonstrating its effectiveness relative to them.
is_compared.quote: Empirically, using DR3 in conjunction with existing offline RL methods provides about 60% performance improvement on the harder D4RL tasks.

referenced_paper_title.justification: DR3 is introduced in this paper and hence does not refer to an existing paper for its concept development.
referenced_paper_title.quote: The explicit regularizer that offsets the difference between the two implicit regularizers is given by... DR3...

name.quote: Empirically, using DR3 in conjunction with existing offline RL methods provides about 60% performance improvement on the harder D4RL (Fu et al., 2020) tasks...
